intro: Research from 2,047 sources and 3,678 claims shows which UI patterns matter most. Each white paper argues one principle with the evidence behind it.

papers.title: The UI base
papers.abstract: What every SISO app rests on: one shell that loads once, one side nav, and a small set of atoms with all their states. We analysed 1,205 pattern types across Carbon, Material 3, Fluent, and Geist, plus 8 side navs we built. The result: 15 rules that cover every component's states.

papers.title: Taste, measured
papers.abstract: What 102,533 rated UI parts say looks good. Editorial and 3D designs rate highest (3.48 and 3.30), well above minimal (2.30 and 2.25). Parts that respond to you beat static ones. The ratings come from a model trained on Refactoring UI and Laws of UX, and nobody else has this dataset.

papers.title: Pages that tell the truth
papers.abstract: How a SISO page is laid out and how it reports state. Pages are bands: glance (KPIs), work (tables and filters), detail (sheets and expansions). Data goes in widgets, which load in place. The hard part: four distinct states for loading, empty, stale, and broken.

papers.title: Built for the mind
papers.abstract: Why people act, decide, and come back: first impressions in 50 ms, choice and defaults, goal-gradient and endowed progress. Large A/B tests measured speed (46% bounce reduction), forms (27% completion gain), and search cues. Dark patterns are charted so you know where the line sits.

papers.title: Built by agents
papers.abstract: A design system an AI can follow: principles as machine-readable data, take-before-you-build, ui-pick command.

papers.title: Words on screens
papers.abstract: Say it once, in fewer words: content design, plain language, scanning hierarchy from Stripe and GOV.UK.

papers.title: Motion with a job
papers.abstract: Movement that explains change, not decoration: easing curves, duration, and reduced-motion from Material 3 and Apple HIG.

papers.title: Tokens and themes
papers.abstract: One set of tokens, many looks: semantic colors, type scale, spacing, elevation, and theming from Geist, Polaris, and Carbon.

findings.title: Skeleton screens cut bounce rates
findings.finding: 32% bounce reduction with skeletons vs spinners; 47% more likely to wait.

findings.title: Specific error messages lift form completion
findings.finding: 27% increase in form completion with specific, aligned error messages.

findings.title: Speed pays in conversion
findings.finding: 26% LCP + 72% FID reduction led to 46% bounce, 87% pages/session, 5% conversion.

findings.title: Defaults shape behavior
findings.finding: Default feature selection increases after earlier choices deplete mental resources.

findings.title: Progress bars drive retention
findings.finding: 2.4x higher Day-1 retention for users with 7+ day streaks.

findings.title: Upfront pricing prevents cart abandonment
findings.finding: Showing fees upfront: 21% less spending, 14.1% less likely to complete.

findings.title: Touch targets need space
findings.finding: Minimum 44 pixels by 44 pixels for touch targets to prevent misses.

findings.title: Aesthetics shape first impressions
findings.finding: People form UI judgments in under 50 milliseconds; aesthetics improve perceived usability.

findings.title: Color-blind design reaches 8.4% of males
findings.finding: Color-blindness affects 8% of males and 0.4% of women.

findings.title: Responsive design improves mobile orders
findings.finding: Responsive layout on mobile: +5.8% orders on tested sites.
